h: Brokenhearted Humility Repairs the Pride Behind Sin

p: צַו אֶת אַהֲרֹן וְאֶת בָּנָיו לֵאמוֹר
this is the law of the olah'?
will in the end go into fire,
as it says, 'It is the olah on its pyre.'"
And its answer is lacking in understanding
of the opening of the section, "Command Aharon."
Now in Midrash Rabbah (beginning of this parsha, Vayikra Rabbah 7:1):
this is what the pasuk says (Mishlei 10:12):
between Yisrael and their Father in Heaven
stirred up against them judgments upon judgments.
Know that there is nothing to it.
This is what Moshe said to Aharon:
"What did this people do to you?"
It would have been better for them
to be judged as unintentional sinners
comes to atone for thoughts of the heart,
כִּדְאִיתָא בִּירוּשַׁלְמִי (יוֹמָא פֶּרֶק ח הֲלָכָה ז)
as it says in the Yerushalmi (Yoma 8:7)
and in Midrash Rabbah (this parsha, Vayikra Rabbah 7:3);
yet HaKadosh Baruch Hu does not
for the thought of a sin,
except for the thought of idolatry,
But we find in the Gemara (Sotah 4b):
כָּל אָדָם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ גַּסּוּת הָרוּחַ
is as though he worships idols."
It turns out that for a thought of arrogance
as for a thought of idolatry.
that Aharon is the groomsman of the Queen,
that regarding something forbidden by the Torah
and one is obligated to rebuke
and inform his fellow of the prohibition;
that he was obligated to inform them
that it is "offerings to the dead."
For about the act of the Calf itself
he said, "Better the sin be attributed to me"
and also it was not clear
that it was for the sake of idolatry,
but regarding their offering Aharon reasoned
that it was clear to all
that it was an idolatrous offering,
to judge them favorably in this;
and therefore he took their offering
peace be upon him, rebuked him,
that it would have been better that they be as unintentional sinners.
For we find even greater than this
regarding Menashe, when he killed Yeshayahu the prophet:
"He judged him and killed him," etc.;
that he will not accept what I tell him,
I will make him an intentional sinner," etc.
And there the prohibition of bloodshed
only, since according to his error
he did not want to make him an intentional sinner.
So too here, Aharon should have
only because of a trace of self-elevation
שֶׁזֶּה הָאִיסּוּר הוּא מְבוֹרָר כָּל כָּךְ
that this prohibition was so clear
therefore he crushed it before them.
מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם עַל זֹאת
peace be upon him, rebuked him about this,
his heart was utterly broken within him
that such a thing happened through him,
which is the opposite of his level,
to always argue in defense of Yisrael,
and in the end the corruption came about through him.
And because of the greatness of his brokenness of spirit
that this parsha be said through him:
this is the law of the olah,"
to atone for the thought of the heart
And this is how the Midrash Rabbah concludes,
שֶׁנִּתְפַּלֵּל מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם עָלָיו כוּ׳
that Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him, prayed for him, etc.:
and its waters are dear," etc.;
HaKadosh Baruch Hu said to him:
"By your life, for your sake, etc.,
אֶלָּא שֶׁאֲנִי עוֹשֶׂה אוֹתוֹ עִיקָּר כוּ׳
but I will make him the main one," etc.
And with this one can understand
"when Nasan the prophet came to him,
when he had gone to Bas Sheva";
and he established the yoke of teshuvah;
his teshuvah would have been complete
רַק לִפְנֵי עֵינֵי דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
but in the eyes of David HaMelech, peace be upon him,
in that he said before Hashem Yisbarach,
and this was from a trace of haughtiness,
that "his heart was hollow within him"
and he did not fear the yetzer hara,
"do not bring me to a test";
כְּאִלּוּ בָּא עַל כָּל הָעֲרָיוֹת כוּ׳
is as though he had relations with all the forbidden women," etc.
his heart was broken within him
(in the Commentary on the Mishnah, Avos 4:4):
a person should go in the middle path,
except for the trait of pride,
where he should lower himself to the furthest extreme.
אַהֲרֹן וְדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בְּנַפְשָׁם
and David HaMelech, peace be upon him, worked upon themselves
to be humbled in the utmost lowliness,
so that there not remain in them
any trace of self-elevation from then on,
not even an eighth of an eighth,
none of it and not part of it
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (שְׁמוֹת טז, ז; בְּמִדְבַּר טז, יא)
for he had no existence at all
וְעַל זֶה אָמַר דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
And about this David HaMelech, peace be upon him, said:
(תְּהִלִּים נא, יח) כִּי לֹא תַחְפּוֹץ זֶבַח וְאֶתֵּנָה
(Tehillim 51:18) "For You do not desire a sacrifice, else I would give it;
You do not want an olah."
For although he was obligated to bring an olah
for the heart's thought of haughtiness,
in the days of Nov and Givon,
at the time when bamos were permitted,
according to the view of Rabbi Shimon,
"The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit,"
as though he offered all the offerings."
And with this (the Midrash Rabbah) concludes:
in Your favor to Tziyon, etc.,
that an olah be actually offered
to atone for the heart's thought of pride.
And this is the intent of the answer of (the Midrash Tanchuma):
"this is the law of the olah":
one who raises himself up before Me,
"it is the olah on its pyre":
that the trait of pride be burned out
none of it and not part of it.
And therefore the opening of the section is

paragraphs.text: Source of the quoted words: Vayikra 6:2 — “צו את אהרן ואת בניו לאמר זאת תורת העלה הוא העלה על מוקדה על המזבח כל הלילה עד הבקר ואש המזבח תוקד בו” — “Command Aaron and his sons thus: This is the ritual of the burnt offering: The burnt offering itself shall remain where it is burned upon the altar all night until morning, while the fire on the altar is kept going …”
